INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Independent Contractor Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of April 6, 2026 (the "Effective Date") by and between Tallowfield Studio LLC, a limited liability company with its principal office at 18 Brennock Lane, Westerley ("Client"), and Dana Orlecki, an individual residing at 302 Hesketh Avenue, Carrow Mills ("Contractor"). Client and Contractor are each referred to in this Agreement as a "Party" and together as the "Parties".

1. Definitions

"Services" means the copywriting, editing, and content strategy work described in one or more statements of work signed by both Parties (each a "Statement of Work"). "Deliverables" means the written materials, content plans, and related documents that Contractor prepares specifically for Client and delivers to Client in performing the Services. "Pre-existing Materials" means any writing, templates, methods, tools, know-how, or other materials that Contractor created or acquired before the Effective Date or outside the Services. "Confidential Information" means any non-public business, technical, or financial information that one Party discloses to the other in connection with this Agreement and that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential. "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, or a public holiday in the place where the receiving Party is located.

2. Services

Contractor shall perform the Services described in each Statement of Work with reasonable skill and care. Each Statement of Work will describe the Services, the Deliverables, the schedule, and the fees for that engagement. If a Statement of Work conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls. Contractor shall determine the method, details, and means of performing the Services. Client shall give Contractor the information, access, and feedback that Contractor reasonably needs to perform the Services on schedule, and any delay caused by Client extends the schedule by the same period.

3. Fees and Payment

Client shall pay Contractor the fees set out in the applicable Statement of Work, and those fees do not change during the term of that Statement of Work unless both Parties agree in writing. Contractor may submit invoices at any time after the Services they cover have been performed. Client shall pay each invoice within fourteen (14) days of receiving it, and payment is not conditioned on acceptance of any Deliverable, on Client's receipt of payment from any third party, or on any other event. If Client disputes part of an invoice in good faith, Client shall pay the undisputed portion on time and the Parties shall work together promptly to resolve the disputed portion. Client shall reimburse reasonable expenses that it approves in writing before Contractor incurs them. Each Party is responsible for its own taxes.

4. Intellectual Property

Contractor retains all right, title, and interest in its Pre-existing Materials, and nothing in this Agreement assigns any Pre-existing Materials to Client. Ownership of each Deliverable passes to Client when Client has paid in full the fees for that Deliverable. To the extent a Deliverable incorporates Pre-existing Materials, Contractor grants Client a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use those Pre-existing Materials as part of that Deliverable. Contractor may display the Deliverables in Contractor's portfolio and website and describe its work for Client.

5. Confidentiality

Each Party shall hold the other Party's Confidential Information in confidence and shall use it only to perform or receive the Services. Neither Party shall disclose the other Party's Confidential Information to any third party without that Party's prior written consent. These obligations do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving Party, that the receiving Party already knew before disclosure, that the receiving Party receives lawfully from a third party without a duty of confidence, or that the receiving Party develops independently. A Party may disclose Confidential Information when required by law or court order, provided that it gives the other Party prompt written notice where the law allows it. The obligations in this Section continue for two (2) years after this Agreement ends.

6. Limitation of Liability

Each Party's total liability to the other Party arising out of or relating to this Agreement is limited to the total fees paid and payable under this Agreement, except that this limit does not apply to Client's obligation to pay fees owed to Contractor. Neither Party is liable to the other for any indirect or consequential loss arising out of this Agreement, and fees owed to Contractor under this Agreement are not indirect or consequential loss. Nothing in this Agreement limits either Party's liability for fraud or for any liability that cannot be limited by law.

7. Freedom to Work

Nothing in this Agreement restricts Contractor from providing services to other clients, including clients in the same industry as Client, during or after the term of this Agreement. Each Party remains free to hire or engage any person, including any person who has worked for the other Party.

8. Term and Termination

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and ends when the Services under every Statement of Work are complete, and it does not renew automatically. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason on fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other Party. On any termination, Client shall pay Contractor for all Services performed up to the effective date of termination, and if Client terminates for convenience, Client shall also pay a termination fee equal to ten percent (10%) of the fees remaining under the current Statement of Work. Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to cure it within ten (10) Business Days after receiving written notice describing the breach. Sections 4, 5, 6, and 10 survive the end of this Agreement.

9. Independent Contractor

Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee, partner, or agent of Client. Nothing in this Agreement creates an employment relationship, partnership, or joint venture between the Parties. Contractor is not entitled to any employee benefits from Client. Neither Party has authority to bind the other Party to any contract or obligation.

10. Governing Law and Disputes

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the state in which Contractor resides. Either Party may bring an action arising out of or relating to this Agreement in any court of competent jurisdiction in the county where Contractor resides, and nothing in this Agreement requires either Party to arbitrate any dispute.

11. Notices

All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by recognized courier, or by email with confirmation of transmission, to the address set out in the opening paragraph of this Agreement or to any other address that a Party designates by notice. A notice is effective on the day it is delivered, or if delivered after 5:00 p.m. local time or on a day that is not a Business Day, on the next Business Day.

12. General

This Agreement, together with each Statement of Work, is the entire agreement between the Parties about its subject matter and supersedes all prior proposals, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral. This Agreement may be amended only by a written document signed by both Parties, and neither Party may change its terms alone. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect. A Party's failure to enforce any provision is not a waiver of its right to enforce that provision later. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, and all counterparts together form one agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
